claims: For the same original smooth unforced periodic NS gradient, k=|adj A|/Q is equivalent to d. Its Kato equation retains a nonnegative zero-set measure, positive cofactor-direction dissipation and a signed remainder controlled by sqrt(3) times GD's full-gradient direction entropy.
An ambient adjugate derivative and Cayley-Hamilton identity bound the inertial source by C d^2. Pressure has the inherited total L1 bound, not an autonomous relative quadratic bound.

The C1,1 regularization sqrt(k^2+delta^2)-delta handles J=0 and Q=0 together without discarding their limiting measure. Lk is a finite signed measure and k dx has a unique finite nonnegative weak endpoint trace in the stated finite-time smooth-solution scope.
A compatible periodic initial jet has vanishing cofactor-direction dissipation while |grad sqrt(k)|^2/(P_k+G) is unbounded. A zero-crossing initial slice need not have sqrt(k) in H1_loc.

An explicit smooth periodic divergence-free initial family has whole-cell signed pressure production epsilon times a strictly positive coefficient, while the integral of d^2 is O(epsilon^2). Uniform local strong theory, an explicit high-order difference estimate and a regular-zero-set argument extend this mismatch to fixed time windows, including fixed positive-age windows.
limitations: No arbitrary-data global regularity, singularity, novelty certification, optimal constants, human peer review or Clay solution.
No strong L1 endpoint trace, exclusion of concentration, or GD.11 critical d norm has been derived.

The pressure counterexample changes initial data with epsilon and refutes only the specified purely quadratic bounds having no extra initial-data term, linear background-coupling term or other compensation on the right. The constant may still depend on the fixed background parameters and common smoothness bound. It is not a single-solution singular-endpoint theorem.
The initial-slice amplitude obstruction does not refute all positive-time cumulative estimates. A Kato zero-set measure is not the divergent ordinary Fisher density.
The exact linearized pressure operator, the component that contributes to actual vorticity stretching, and any useful joint estimate still require a separate derivation and review.
No public overview, website, local reader, public counts, recap, attachments or relaunch requested.
